resolved_stage_spec.notes: Section 21 CDCC adult/disabled-dependent care inputs (PolicyEngine/microcosm#451 item 1), previously structural zeros in both the retired eCPS and every Microcosm base. Source decision receipts (Census API variable dictionaries, ASEC 2024 and SIPP 2023, read 2026-07-22): ASEC carries the qualifying concept directly - person item PEDISDRS ('difficulty dressing or bathing') operationalizes 'physically or mentally incapable of self-care', with SIPP's identical ESELFCARE item corroborating; NEITHER instrument's current public-use release carries in-household adult-care expenditures: ASEC's only care-expense items are childcare HCHCARE_VAL/SPM_CHILDCAREXPNS, and while the 2018 SIPP panel's Child & Dependent Care topical module collected paid dependent-care fields (ECREPAYANYON, TDEPNDNTEXP), they are absent from the 2023 SIPP PUF dictionary (the pinned donor vintage), whose only adult-care payment amount TDPCAREAMT covers care of a former household member, failing section 21's same-principal-abode requirement. The dollar leg is therefore an explicitly documented same-instrument proxy: the measured ASEC work-related childcare expense distribution (the same section 21 employment-related expense class, subject to the same 26 USC 21(c) per-person cap) supplies the paid-care usage rate and the positive level distribution (weighted quantiles, zero-weight donors excluded). The donor universe is measured at SPM-unit grain, where the childcare leaf lives: units with any member under the 21(b)(1)(A) age limit and any positive member earnings, on the measured ASEC channel - an approximation of the binding childcare population at donor grain, not a reproduction of the tax-unit minimum-earnings test. Recipient support is restricted to tax units where the statute can bind: a measured disabled qualifying individual under 21(b)(1)(B) (dependent) or 21(b)(1)(C) (married head or spouse), plus the 21(d) earnings structure computed exactly as the engine's min_head_spouse_earned binds - both spouses earning, or a 21(d)(2) floor-eligible spouse (incapable of self-care, or the measured full-time college student via is_full_time_college_student) deemed while the OTHER spouse actually earns; deeming never rescues a unit whose only earner is the floor-eligible spouse. Selection is a seeded weight-targeted permutation prefix over sorted unit ids (invariant to person-row order) at the measured usage rate; levels are a distribution-preserving weighted-quantile draw whose grid is the selected units' own cumulative-weight midpoints, placed on the qualifying person with the smallest person_id. PolicyEngine-US 1.764.6 owns all downstream CDCC formulas; is_incapable_of_self_care is also read by SNAP/Medicaid work-requirement exemptions and state CDCC analogs, which move those programs from flag-off defaults toward the measured disability structure.

resolved_stage_spec.notes: Section 21 CDCC adult/disabled-dependent care inputs (PolicyEngine/microcosm#451 item 1), previously structural zeros in both the retired eCPS and every Microcosm base. Source decision receipts (Census API variable dictionaries, ASEC 2024 and SIPP 2023, read 2026-07-22): ASEC carries the qualifying concept directly - person item PEDISDRS ('difficulty dressing or bathing') operationalizes 'physically or mentally incapable of self-care', with SIPP's identical ESELFCARE item corroborating; NEITHER instrument's current public-use release carries in-household adult-care expenditures: ASEC's only care-expense items are childcare HCHCARE_VAL/SPM_CHILDCAREXPNS, and while the 2018 SIPP panel's Child & Dependent Care topical module collected paid dependent-care fields (ECREPAYANYON, TDEPNDNTEXP), they are absent from the 2023 SIPP PUF dictionary (the pinned donor vintage), whose only adult-care payment amount TDPCAREAMT covers care of a former household member, failing section 21's same-principal-abode requirement. The dollar leg is therefore an explicitly documented same-instrument proxy: the measured ASEC work-related childcare expense distribution (the same section 21 employment-related expense class, subject to the same 26 USC 21(c) per-person cap) supplies the paid-care usage rate and the positive level distribution (weighted quantiles, zero-weight donors excluded). The donor universe is measured at SPM-unit grain, where the childcare leaf lives: units with any member under the 21(b)(1)(A) age limit and any positive member earnings, on the measured ASEC channel - an approximation of the binding childcare population at donor grain, not a reproduction of the tax-unit minimum-earnings test. Recipient support is restricted to tax units where the statute can bind: a measured disabled qualifying individual under 21(b)(1)(B) (dependent) or 21(b)(1)(C) (married head or spouse), plus the 21(d) earnings structure computed exactly as the engine's min_head_spouse_earned binds - both spouses earning, or a 21(d)(2) floor-eligible spouse (incapable of self-care, or the measured full-time college student via is_full_time_college_student) deemed while the OTHER spouse actually earns; deeming never rescues a unit whose only earner is the floor-eligible spouse. Selection is a seeded weight-targeted permutation prefix over sorted unit ids (invariant to person-row order) at the measured usage rate; levels are a distribution-preserving weighted-quantile draw whose grid is the selected units' own cumulative-weight midpoints, placed on the qualifying person with the smallest person_id. PolicyEngine-US 1.764.6 owns all downstream CDCC formulas; is_incapable_of_self_care is also read by SNAP/Medicaid work-requirement exemptions and state CDCC analogs, which move those programs from flag-off defaults toward the measured disability structure.
